I'm genuinely surprised how many people still don't know the different types of AI.

Here's the complete AI roadmap that explains every major type of AI in one simple visual.

---

1. AI can be classified based on capabilities, functionality, learning, purpose, input, autonomy, and industry.

---

2. Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI) is the only type of AI that exists today.

---

3. Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) aims to match human-level intelligence but has not been achieved yet.

---

4. Artificial Superintelligence (ASI) is still hypothetical and does not exist.

---

5. Reactive Machines only respond to current inputs and cannot learn from experience.

---

6. Limited Memory AI learns from past data and powers most modern AI systems like ChatGPT.

---

7. Theory of Mind AI could understand human emotions and intentions but remains in research.

---

8. Self-Aware AI would possess consciousness and self-awareness but is purely hypothetical.

---

9. Supervised Learning trains AI using labeled data for tasks like spam detection and image classification.

---

10. Unsupervised Learning finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data for clustering and anomaly detection.

---

11. Semi-Supervised Learning combines labeled and unlabeled data to improve learning.

---

12. Self-Supervised Learning creates its own labels and powers many modern foundation models.

---

13. Reinforcement Learning teaches AI through rewards and penalties to improve decisions.

---

14. Deep Learning uses neural networks for complex tasks involving vision, speech, and language.

---

15. Generative AI creates new content including text, images, videos, audio, and code.

---

16. Predictive AI forecasts future outcomes such as sales and risk predictions.

---

17. Analytical AI extracts insights from existing data to support better decisions.

---

18. AI can also be categorized by input, including text, image, audio, video, and multimodal AI.

---

19. Modern AI systems range from AI assistants and copilots to autonomous AI agents and multi-agent systems.

---

20. AI is rapidly evolving from rule-based systems to generative and agentic AI, with AGI and ASI remaining future possibilities.

---

I think one reason the usage of AI agents hasn’t fully broken through yet is that the platforms built around them still present a fairly narrow view of what they can be used for and more importantly don’t do enough to inspire curiosity among the general public about what they can do with it.

Most tools showcase their capabilities through packaged workflows like write this, research that, generate an image or complete this task.

Those might be useful, but they make agents feel like a collection of separate tools for separate jobs. You get an output and move on. The platforms and their demos dont do enough to help the average person see how these capabilities could be combined, adapted, or turned into something entirely different.

The platforms environment plays a massive role in this imo.  If the environment through which agents are called and their work is consumed is mostly a chat box, a wall of text, or a one-off artifact, then even a highly capable system can feel narrow. You experience the output, but not the larger creative and operational space behind it.

The more powerful experience might be when a platform lets you move fluidly between different modes:

→ an idea into a visual
→ a visual into a prototype
→ a prototype into a deployed experience
→ a repeated action into a skill
→ a skill into an automation
→ an external tool into a larger workflow

That changes your relationship with AI. You move from thinking “what task can this tool complete?” but rather start feeling, “what can I make this environment do?”

I feel like @dexto_ai is one of the few products moving in this direction well.

The biggest unlock for me wasn’t discovering that the models had suddenly become more capable. It was using Dexto that made more of that capability available, connected, and easy to experiment with. 

AI adoption won’t fully happen when models become capable enough. It will happen when platforms become good enough at making that capability feel visible, personal, and endlessly explorable.

Today, we are announcing Arena's factuality leaderboards, which evaluate the objective performance of AI models in reality and guard against hallucinations.

Arena's chat leaderboard has historically focused on human preference. Although our style control methodology adjusts for the effect of emojis, response length, and other stylistic factors, we wanted a more direct way of measuring objective signals of chatbot utility and anti-hallucination.

Hence, we developed the factuality leaderboards, which speak to the fraction of correct factual claims that a model makes. We basically extract all factual claims and cross-reference them against the internet to ensure they are based in evidence. Models that are supporting their claims with stronger evidence get a better score, and this gives a strong basis for objective performance beyond preference alone.

The big winners, as you can see on this plot, are OpenAI and Grok. Notably, Claude models, as well as Ernie and Muse-Spark-1.1, decrease in ranking.

Rather than optimizing a diffusion policy with unstable RL objectives, EvoHIL combines a self-evolving reward model with flow matching optimization.

The policy learns from better rewards, while better policies generate stronger preference data for the next reward update. Each component bootstraps the other.
